title: Canto 12: The Age of Deterioration - Title, Artist and Source Pictures Canto 12
content:
Title, Artist and Source Pictures Canto 12

12.1

Title: The image shows the advisor Cānakya conversing with emperor Maurya.

Artist: Unknown

Source/Courtesy: Vahini.org

12.2

Title: The picture of the Avātar Kalki is a detail of a scroll painting called ‘Dasavatar’,

Andhra Pradesh, 19th century, India

Source: V&A Museum, Wikimedia.org

12.3

Title: The vintage image shows Lord Caitanya dancing for Kṛṣṇa

Artist: Unknown

Source: Internet

12.4

Title: The first painting is of the flood.

Artist: Wassilij Petrovich Wereschtschagin (1835 - 1909).

Source: Internet - Art Catalog Ru

Title: The second painting with title: ‘Light and Colour (Goethe’s Theory) - the Morning

after the Deluge, Moses Writing the Book of Genesis’ (1843)

Artist: Joseph Mallord William Turner

Source: Wikimedia.org

12.5

Title: The image is depicting a soul carried to heaven by two angels

Artist: William Bouguereau

Source: Ocean’s Bridge - Share the Art

12.6

Title: The image of Parīkṣit before Śukadeva is a detail of the image used in Canto 2.8.

It is a Kishangarh painting of the Rajasthani school. India, ± 17th. century.

Source: The Hare Kṛṣṇas, harekrsna.com

The second image is a collage by Anand Aadhar against the background of a painting called: "Yantra of Lord Viṣṇu with twenty-four Avatāras".

Artist: Vidya Devi and Dhirendra Jha.

Source: © Exotic India, exoticindiaart.com (used with permission)

12.7

Title: The image represents a couple of Śrīmad Bhāgavatam pages.

Source: Internet

12.8

Title: The image is a detail from a painting titled: ‘Sage Mārkaṇḍeya’s Ashram and the Milky Ocean’, folio from the Durga Charit. Attributed to the “Durga Master”, Jodhpur, ca. 1780-90.

Source: Meharangarh Museum Trust.

12.9

Title: The vintage image shows infant Kṛṣṇa holding His foot.

Artist: Unknown

Source: Internet

12.10

Title: ‘Dance of Śiva’.

Artist: Kithindra Nāth Mazumdar.

Source: ‘Myths of the Hindus and Buddhists’, Ballantine Press, Oct. 1913.

12.11

Title: The first vintage image shows the Universal form of Kṛṣṇa He demonstrated to Arjuna.

Title: The second image is an artist’s impression of Kṛṣṇa as the light in the heart of all mother nature.

Source: Internet

12.12

Title: The first picture is a vintage representation of the Dasāvatāra forms.

Title: ‘Kṛṣṇa and Balarama Swing with Friends’.

Source: © Exotic India, exoticindiaart.com (used with permission).

Title: The third picture of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa privately, is a detail of a classical

Bhāgavata Purāṇa folio.

Source: The Hare Kṛṣṇas, harekrsna.com

12.13

Title: ‘Nārada Muni and Vyāsadev’. Kedar Ragini from Ragmala. Rajasthan Bikaner, c. 1690.

Source: The Hare Kṛṣṇas, harekrsna.com
